newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended lower in quiet dealings as an early rally in New York proved short lived. January finished $14 lower at $1,257 per tonne while March gave up $7 to close at $1,229 per tonne. In New York arabica futures ended a quiet session mixed with front month March giving up 25 points to close at 116.65 cents/lb. May gave up 20 points to close 114.95 cents/lb. The fairly steady tone was linked to fund buying based on improving technicals. However, fundamentally it is expected that supplies of new crop coffee will increase which should keep prices in check. Longer term if the 1997/98 Brazilian crop is small then the market might be able to resume the uptrend, trade sources said.

MALAYSIA - Malaysia imported 391,800 bags of coffee in October/August 1995/96, sharply up from last year's figure of 257,500 bags. Total imports in crop year 1994/95 (October/September) reached 278,300 bags. The main supplier of green coffee in October/August 1995/96 was Indonesia with 237,700 bags up from 123,200 bags the same period in 1994/95.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong imported 137,900 bags of coffee in January/September 1996, 13 per cent more than was imported the same period the previous year. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped sharply by 35 per cent to 156,400 bags. The country gets most of its coffee in the form of solubles from China and South Korea. Hong Kong exported 46,900 bags of coffee in January/September 1996, 45 per cent less than was exported the same period in 1995. Already in calendar year 1995 exports dropped sharply to 120,500 bags down from 227,100 bags exported in 1994. Striking is the sharp fall of soluble exports to the United States which dropped from 69,300 bags in 1994 to 2,700 bags in 1995.
